reading.title: The history of artificial intelligence

sentences.text: Modern artificial intelligence owes much to the development of neural networks and deep learning techniques, which allow machines to learn from vast amounts of data without explicit programming.

The field of artificial intelligence was formally established in 1956 at the Dartmouth Conference, where pioneering researchers came together to explore whether machines could simulate human intelligence.
Early AI systems, such as expert systems developed in the 1970s and 1980s, showed promise but were limited by their inability to handle complexity and adapt to new situations.
Today, AI applications are ubiquitous, powering everything from virtual assistants to medical diagnostic systems, and continuing to reshape industries and society at large.

reading.tip: Start with the historical establishment of AI as a field (B). Progress through the early systems with limitations (C), then modern advances (A), and conclude with current applications (D).

reading.title: The process of photosynthesis

sentences.text: The energy captured from light is used to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose, a simple sugar that plants use for energy and growth.
Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, specialised structures within plant cells that contain the pigment chlorophyll.
During this process, plants also release oxygen as a byproduct, which is essential for most life forms on Earth.
This process begins when chlorophyll absorbs light energy from the sun, converting the light into chemical energy that can be used by the plant.

reading.tip: Introduce the location and mechanism (B), then describe the initial energy capture (D), the conversion process (A), and finally the important byproduct (C).

reading.title: Urban heat island effect

sentences.text: The consequences of the urban heat island effect extend beyond discomfort, as elevated temperatures increase energy consumption for air conditioning and contribute to worsening air quality through increased ozone formation.
This phenomenon, known as the urban heat island effect, occurs when urban areas experience significantly higher temperatures than their surrounding rural regions.

Cities are warmer than surrounding areas because buildings, roads, and other infrastructure absorb and retain solar radiation, while trees and vegetation that would normally provide cooling are often absent in densely built areas.
Cities worldwide are implementing strategies such as increasing green spaces, installing reflective roofing materials, and promoting urban forests to mitigate the urban heat island effect.

reading.tip: Define the phenomenon first (B), explain the scientific cause (C), then discuss the consequences (A), and finally present solutions (D).

reading.title: The evolution of mobile technology

sentences.text: The introduction of smartphones with touchscreen technology and mobile applications fundamentally changed how people interact with technology, providing access to communication, information, and entertainment in the palm of their hand.

Mobile phones began as large, cumbersome devices designed primarily for voice communication, but decades of technological advancement have transformed them into indispensable tools that influence nearly every aspect of modern life.

Today, mobile devices have evolved to include advanced features such as high-resolution cameras, artificial intelligence assistants, and wearable connectivity, further expanding their role in daily life.

The transition from basic mobile phones to early smartphones in the late 2000s marked a turning point, as these devices began to incorporate internet connectivity and limited application capabilities.

reading.tip: Begin with the historical context of early phones (B), transition to early smartphones (D), describe the revolution of touchscreen technology (A), then conclude with modern advanced features (C).

reading.title: The role of wetlands in ecosystems

sentences.text: Wetlands are also significant carbon sinks, storing vast amounts of carbon in their soils and vegetation, making them crucial in efforts to combat climate change and reduce atmospheric carbon dioxide levels.

Wetlands are among the most biologically productive ecosystems on Earth, supporting diverse plant and animal communities that depend on the unique conditions created by seasonal flooding and nutrient-rich waters.
Beyond their role as biodiversity hotspots, wetlands provide invaluable services such as water filtration, flood prevention, and coastal protection by absorbing excess water during heavy rainfall.

Despite their importance, wetlands are rapidly disappearing due to human development and drainage for agriculture, resulting in significant losses of habitat and ecosystem services that took millennia to develop.

reading.tip: Introduce the ecological productivity of wetlands (B), discuss their ecosystem services (C), highlight their climate benefits (A), and conclude with the threat they face (D).

reading.title: The development of antibiotics

sentences.text: The discovery of penicillin in 1928 by Alexander Fleming revolutionised medicine by providing the first effective treatment for bacterial infections, transforming antibiotics into one of the most valuable tools in modern healthcare.
Before this discovery, bacterial infections posed serious health risks, and many diseases that are now easily treatable were once life-threatening and often fatal.

However, decades of overuse and misuse of antibiotics in medical and agricultural settings have led to the emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, a development that now threatens to reverse the gains made in treating infectious diseases.

Medical researchers continue to develop new antibiotics and alternative treatments to combat resistance, recognising that this challenge requires ongoing innovation and careful stewardship of existing medications.

reading.tip: Begin with the historical context of infectious diseases (B), describe the breakthrough discovery (A), then present the modern challenge of resistance (C), and finally discuss current responses (D).
